description:
Estimates year-one federal + state tax savings from operating a property as a short-term rental, leveraging the 'STR loophole' (cost segregation + bonus depreciation + active-income offset when material participation requirements are met).

Returns: `firstYearSavings` (the savings the user actually gets in year one — the active-income offset only when the loophole applies, otherwise the passive treatment, which is usually $0 with no other passive income), `potentialSavingsIfQualified` (the active-offset figure if they did qualify), `qualifies` (boolean — does the situation qualify for the active-income loophole), `bonusDepreciation`, `totalDepreciation`, `paperLoss`, `combinedMarginalRate`, `passiveCarryforward`, plus any `warnings` the calculator surfaced, and echoed inputs (`marginalBracketPct`, `propertyPrice`, `yearPlacedInService`).

The estimator uses standard cost-segregation component ratios (20% personal property / 10% land improvements / 70% structure) and current bonus depreciation rates by year placed in service. Operating numbers (revenue, opex, mortgage interest) are derived from typical STR heuristics — 8% gross revenue / 40% opex ratio / 75% LTV / 7.5% rate / 30y term — so the caller only needs to provide the purchase price and tax profile. This is an underwriting illustration, NOT a substitute for a cost-segregation study or CPA advice. **Always tell the user to consult a CPA before relying on this.**

Use this tool when the user wants to understand the after-tax cash impact of buying a property as an STR, is evaluating whether the STR loophole applies, or is comparing acquisition tax outcomes across price points.

Required: `purchase_price`, `year_placed_in_service` (2025, 2026, or 2027), `marginal_tax_bracket` (one of 0.22, 0.24, 0.32, 0.35, 0.37), `avg_guest_stay_days` (1-30; the loophole requires 7 days or less), `materially_participates` (boolean — true only if the user will spend 100+ hours/year managing AND that's more than anyone else; ask the user to confirm before assuming true). Optional: `state_marginal_rate` (default 0), `land_value_percent` (default 0.20).

No STRvest account needed. To save results or run full underwriting, the user can create a free account at https://strvest.com/sign-up and connect the authenticated STRvest MCP server (https://strvest.com/mcp).

avg_guest_stay_days.description: Expected average length of guest stays in days. The STR loophole requires this to be 7 days or less (otherwise it counts as long-term rental, not STR). Typical STR averages 3-5 days; ski / beach destinations skew toward 5-7.

land_value_percent.description: Optional. Land's share of total purchase price as a decimal — depreciable basis = purchase price × (1 − this). Default 0.20 reflects typical suburban single-family. Lower for condos / land-light properties, higher for primarily-land properties.

marginal_tax_bracket.description: User's federal marginal income tax bracket as a decimal (NOT a percent). Allowed values: 0.22, 0.24, 0.32, 0.35, 0.37. If the user gives you a percent (e.g. '32%'), convert to 0.32. Ask the user what bracket they're in — don't guess.

materially_participates.description: Whether the user will materially participate in the rental business. IRS test: 100+ hours per year AND more than anyone else, OR 500+ hours total. Required for the loophole to convert paper loss into an active-income offset. If the user has a property manager doing most of the work, this is false. Ask before assuming true.

purchase_price.description: Property purchase price in US dollars. REQUIRED. Example: 850000 for $850,000.

state_marginal_rate.description: Optional. State marginal income tax rate as a decimal (not a percent). Defaults to 0 (federal-only display).

year_placed_in_service.description: Calendar year the property will first be rented as an STR. Only 2025, 2026, and 2027 are supported — bonus depreciation rates change by year.
